extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in UK media, journalism ethics, and legal investigations
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive Wikipedia encyclopedia entry summarising the News International / News of the World phone-hacking scandal, its investigations, legal actions, key events, and public/political fallout. Intended as a factual, sourced timeline and background on the affair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offence of accessing voicemail under Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000 (s.79)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessing voicemail messages is an offence under section 79 of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article recounts arrests and convictions (e.g., Clive Goodman and Glenn Mulcaire) for hacking voicemail under this provision; it is cited as the statutory basis for criminal charges relating to voicemail interception.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC position on use of subterfuge / public interest defence
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a legitimate place for the use of subterfuge when there are grounds in the public interest to use it and it is not possible to obtain information through other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the Press Complaints Commission's stated standard in its 2007 inquiry quoted by the article; the PCC nonetheless recommended that the practice should stop. The article uses this formulation to frame debates about journalistic ethics versus illegal activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegal means of gaining information (enumerated list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illegal means included hacking private voicemail accounts, hacking into computers, making false statements to officials, entrapment, blackmail, burglaries, theft of mobile phones and making payments to public officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists these methods as examples of unlawful information-gathering used by private investigators and journalists; they are treated as indicators of criminal or unethical newsgathering practices that triggered investigations (ICO, Met, CPS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unregistered personal-information databases and unlawful trade in confidential data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Information Commissioner's Office operation (Operation Motorman) uncovered personal information kept on unregistered computer databases and invoices showing newspapers purchasing confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as establishing that confidential information was illegally acquired from telephone companies, the DVLA and the Police National Computer; the ICO reports ('What price privacy?') are cited as documenting the practice and the scale (thousands of requests), and used to justify further scrutiny and prosecutions of private investigators.
